$doc: Vyomi capability registry — RDS. See s3.json for the contract.

rds.instance.deletion-protection.title: Deletion protection
limitations: ModifyDBInstance applies a fixed subset of fields (class, storage, engine version, backup retention, master password); other settings are stored and returned but not individually validated.

rds.data-api.title: SQL execution (Query editor / RDS Data API)
limitations: The data plane is a real engine (sqlite3 by default, PGlite real Postgres on Nano) reached only through the RDS Data API (ExecuteStatement/BatchExecuteStatement) — Vyomi does not expose the Postgres/MySQL wire protocol directly, so an unmodified psycopg2/mysqlclient TCP connection cannot reach it.
Transactions are accepted (BeginTransaction/CommitTransaction/RollbackTransaction) for SDK compatibility, but each statement autocommits — there is no cross-call rollback yet.

rds.subnet-groups.title: DB subnet groups
limitations: Subnet IDs and the VPC are stored and returned exactly as given; Vyomi does not validate that they exist in a real VPC (it does not model EC2/VPC in depth for RDS).

rds.parameter-groups.title: DB parameter groups and parameters
limitations: Parameters are stored and returned exactly as modified (ModifyDBParameterGroup round-trips through DescribeDBParameters), but Vyomi does not apply them to the SQL engine — the data plane's real behaviour (e.g. max_connections) is unaffected.

rds.events.title: Events (DescribeEvents)
limitations: Vyomi logs its own control-plane actions (create/modify/delete/lifecycle/snapshot); it does not generate the full category list AWS produces (e.g. failover, low-storage).

rds.proxy.title: RDS Proxy
limitations: Creating, listing and deleting a DB proxy record is real and stateful; Vyomi does not actually proxy connections through it — apps still connect straight to the instance's own endpoint.

rds.option-groups.title: Option groups
limitations: Option group metadata CRUD is real; adding/removing individual options within a group is not modeled — Vyomi has no engine-specific option catalogue (e.g. Oracle APEX, SQL Server TDE).

rds.event-subscriptions.title: Event subscriptions
limitations: Subscription metadata CRUD is real; Vyomi never actually publishes a notification to the SNS topic when a matching event occurs.

rds.automated-backups.title: Automated backups
limitations: The current-region automated backup window is derived from the live instance's retention setting (DescribeDBInstanceAutomatedBackups); cross-region replication of backups and backups retained after instance deletion are not modeled.

rds.monitoring.title: CloudWatch metrics on the DB instance detail page
limitations: Vyomi does not emit CPUUtilization/DatabaseConnections/IOPS metrics for RDS instances, so the Monitoring tab has nothing real to chart.

rds.logs.title: DB log files
limitations: The sqlite3 / PGlite data plane does not produce real engine log files (error log, slow query log) for Vyomi to list or tail.

rds.replication.title: Read replicas, Multi-AZ failover, connected compute resources, security group rules
limitations: Vyomi does not model a second physical replica, EC2 instances, or VPC security group rule evaluation for RDS; MultiAZ/compute-resource fields are stored and returned but have no runtime effect.

rds.reserved-instances.title: Reserved instances (purchase)
limitations: PurchaseReservedDBInstancesOffering records a real, stateful reservation (DescribeReservedDBInstances lists it); Vyomi has no billing system and no reserved-instance-offering catalogue, so the console's purchase wizard (pricing, terms, offering ids) is not built — call the action directly with a reservation id.

rds.capacity-reservations.title: Capacity reservations
limitations: Capacity reservations are a capacity-market/billing construct Vyomi does not model.

rds.zero-etl.title: Zero-ETL integrations
limitations: CreateIntegration/DeleteIntegration/DescribeIntegrations is real, stateful metadata CRUD; Vyomi does not run the actual cross-service replication pipeline into Redshift, so the console's create wizard (picking a real Redshift target) is not built — call the action directly with source/target ARNs.

rds.custom-engine-versions.title: RDS Custom engine versions
limitations: CreateCustomDBEngineVersion/DeleteCustomDBEngineVersion/DescribeDBEngineVersions registers real, stateful install-media metadata; RDS Custom itself (the customer-managed EC2 instance the engine actually runs on) is out of Vyomi's scope entirely — the console's create wizard is not built.

rds.recommendations.title: RDS recommendations
limitations: DescribeDBRecommendations derives real advisories from each instance's own live configuration (no Multi-AZ, an outdated CA certificate); Vyomi has no general analysis engine, so it does not generate the full category of recommendations AWS's own monitoring produces (e.g. storage autoscaling, parameter tuning).

rds.exports-to-s3.title: Exports to Amazon S3
limitations: StartExportTask/CancelExportTask/DescribeExportTasks is real, stateful metadata CRUD; Nano has no provisioning lag so a started export completes immediately, and no bytes are actually written to the named S3 bucket.

rds.certificate-rotation.title: Certificate authority rotation
limitations: CACertificateIdentifier is a real, settable field (CreateDBInstance/ModifyDBInstance); any instance whose CA differs from the current default (rds-ca-rsa2048-g1) is flagged on the certificate-update page. Vyomi does not model real CA expiry dates or actually rotate the certificate a connection presents.
